key_insight: The paper compares direct and indirect PINNs for Dirichlet boundary control of semilinear parabolic PDEs and establishes a conditional error analysis for the indirect optimality-system formulation.
engineering_relevance: It provides a principled way to train PINNs for constrained PDE control problems while also yielding a computable residual indicator that can help assess solution quality in practice.
method: Direct PINN: separate state/control networks minimize a penalized tracking objective.
Indirect PINN: joint networks for state, adjoint, and control enforce the first-order optimality system.
Error analysis splits total error into approximation, optimization, quadrature, and soft-constraint terms, with a conditional residual-to-error bound.
evidence_signal: The methods are evaluated on two manufactured test problems: a cubic reaction-diffusion equation and a linear problem with nontrivial boundary control and adjoint.
watch_item: The reliability bound is conditional on regularity, approximation quality, and staying in a local neighborhood of the reference optimal solution, so performance may weaken when soft constraints are hard to satisfy.
paper_title: Direct and Indirect Physics-Informed Neural Networks for Dirichlet Boundary Control of Semilinear Parabolic Equations: A Conditional Error Analysis
